scope: Program contract and bounded omissions; comparison comments remain attributed claims
interface_notes: C22 opens byte production, supplied ELF input and the exact handoff comparisons.
state_owner: the assembler program and its input producer
mechanism: The file consumes described bytes; its header names intended M1/hex2 use and selected comparisons but supplies no ELF envelope.
assumptions: The bounded profile is a fresh Linux/AMD64 seed loading 010 then 130, with 64-bit cells; source comments are not execution evidence.
teaching_section: The boundary we hand to the next chapter

scope: Fresh-load storage relocation and bounded capacity-check helper
interface_notes: C22 reuses asm-check-cap for output and labels.
phase: source loading; capacity checks during all three walks
state_owner: seed dictionary allocation; the caller of each checked append
mechanism: Relocate HERE before large reserves; the shared check receives the occupancy after the proposed write so each caller controls its capacity policy.
assumptions: skip-vm-pages assigns HERE to 0x414000 and requires HERE still below 0x410000; it is not a high-water-mark allocator after arbitrary loads.
declaration_notes: asm-check-cap (colon, L51-L53): consumes proposed occupancy, capacity and exit code; permits equality and exits only when proposed occupancy is greater
initialization_forms: L45: skip-vm-pages sets HERE to 0x414000 before buffer allocation; a load-time initialization form, not a colon definition
teaching_section: Start a separate assembler process

scope: Separate raw/expanded buffers, capacities and lengths
interface_notes: C22 reads the completed expanded buffer without modifying it.
declarations: asm-src-cap; asm-src-buf; asm-src-len; asm-exp-cap; asm-exp-buf; asm-exp-len
phase: source loading allocates; raw load and expansion fill
state_owner: raw input and expanded text, with separate lengths
mechanism: Two 4 MiB buffers separate the bytes borrowed by definition records from the text that later label records borrow.
assumptions: Allocated bytes are not initialized by allot; lengths determine live contents; raw bytes must remain unchanged during expansion.
declaration_notes: asm-src-cap (constant, L57-L57): sets raw-input capacity to 4194304 bytes; asm-src-buf (create, L58-L58): reserves raw-input bytes that own the borrowed definition names and bodies; asm-src-len (variable, L59-L59): holds the number of loaded raw-input bytes, reset before reading; asm-exp-cap (constant, L63-L63): sets expanded-text capacity to 4194304 bytes; asm-exp-buf (create, L64-L64): reserves separate expanded text that later owns borrowed label names; asm-exp-len (variable, L65-L65): holds expanded-text length, reset at expansion start and advanced by byte append
teaching_section: Read the cells and bytes in the implementation

scope: Active cursor state and raw/expanded buffer selection
interface_notes: C22 selects expanded text once before its two assembly passes.
state_owner: the active text cursor
mechanism: Selecting a buffer installs address and length and rewinds position; clients therefore share one reader without sharing the two storage owners.
assumptions: The selected length is copied when selection occurs; it is not an alias to the buffer-length variable.
declaration_notes: asm-cur-buf (variable, L69-L69): holds the selected raw or expanded buffer address; asm-cur-len (variable, L70-L70): holds a snapshot of the selected buffer length; asm-cur-pos (variable, L71-L71): holds the next text-byte index within the selected buffer; asm-use-src (colon, L73-L76): selects the raw buffer and its current length, then starts its cursor at zero; asm-use-exp (colon, L78-L81): selects the completed expanded buffer and length, then starts its cursor at zero
teaching_section: One reader, two selected buffers

scope: Cursor rewind without clearing data or labels
interface_notes: See asm-main in the driver region for the complete reset boundary.
state_owner: cursor position only
mechanism: Rewind selects the same token sequence without clearing label records; IP and output position are reset by separate driver operations.
assumptions: Expanded bytes and selected length remain unchanged.
declaration_notes: asm-reset-pos (colon, L83-L83): sets only cursor position to zero so pass 2 can reread unchanged text without erasing labels
teaching_section: Rewind the reading position, keep the discoveries

scope: Read-to-buffer loop, strict input capacity and nonpositive-read boundary
interface_notes: The expanded/output append policy allows exact capacity and must not be inferred from this stricter load policy.
state_owner: raw buffer and loaded-byte count
mechanism: Positive read counts extend the input; checking length plus one deliberately rejects an exactly full input buffer.
assumptions: A nonpositive read ends the loop without distinguishing EOF from read failure; successful input length is strictly below 4194304.
declaration_notes: asm-load-stdin (colon, L88-L97): fills raw storage from fd 0, adds positive read counts and exits 239 if length plus one exceeds capacity
teaching_section: Capacity means the proposed next length

scope: EOF test, peek and advance cursor contracts
interface_notes: The same words read raw text in C21 and expanded text in C22.
state_owner: active cursor
mechanism: EOF is a position/length predicate; peek observes, while next returns the observation and advances one text byte.
assumptions: Zero from peek alone does not identify EOF because a stored byte can also be zero; callers use asm-eof?.
declaration_notes: asm-eof? (colon, L100-L100): compares cursor position with selected length; position at or beyond length is EOF; asm-peek-char (colon, L103-L108): returns the current byte without advancing, or zero at EOF; asm-next-char (colon, L111-L113): returns the peeked byte and advances the cursor once, including when peek returns the EOF zero
teaching_section: One reader, two selected buffers

scope: Bounded expanded-text append
interface_notes: All ordinary copying and direct-string encoders share this sink.
state_owner: expanded text and its live length
mechanism: A pre-write capacity test prevents the next append from exceeding the reserved region; equality remains allowed.
assumptions: Appending one byte truncates to the stored low byte; over-capacity exits 240 before that write.
declaration_notes: asm-exp-emit-byte (colon, L116-L119): checks prospective expansion length, stores one low byte, then increments that length
teaching_section: Capacity means the proposed next length

scope: Output buffer, reset and checked byte append
interface_notes: C21 owns the common capacity helper; C22 explains the difference between output position and pass-1 IP.
phase: source loading allocates; assembly pass 2 emits
state_owner: output buffer and emitted-byte position
mechanism: Output has its own 1 MiB storage and counter; pass 1 measures with IP without creating placeholder bytes.
assumptions: Exact output capacity is allowed; the next byte fails 241 before storage; zeroing position does not erase existing memory bytes.
declaration_notes: asm-out-cap (constant, L124-L124): sets emitted-output capacity to 1048576 bytes; asm-out-buf (create, L125-L125): reserves output bytes separately from raw and expanded text; asm-out-pos (variable, L126-L126): holds the number of emitted bytes; it is not the pass-1 sizing counter; asm-out-init (colon, L128-L128): resets emitted-byte position to zero before pass 2; asm-emit-byte (colon, L131-L134): checks prospective output position against capacity, writes one low byte and advances position
teaching_section: Reference: a complete buffer is followed by a write attempt

scope: Open/write/close attempt and stderr newline storage
interface_notes: Only asm-main reaches output storage after successful processing of both assembly passes.
state_owner: named output file; diagnostic LF data
mechanism: A negative open result is checked, but the following single write and close have discarded results; token errors reuse the stored LF.
assumptions: Path must be NUL terminated; requested mode 0755 is subject to umask or an existing file mode; a zero exit is not a complete-write witness.
declaration_notes: asm-write-output (colon, L142-L149): opens the supplied NUL-terminated path with flags 577 and requested mode 493, checks negative open results, then attempts one write and close; asm-nl-byte (create, L152-L152): creates the LF byte used after a token diagnostic on fd 2
teaching_section: Reference: a complete buffer is followed by a write attempt

scope: Label record/table storage; target base, IP and pass state
interface_notes: Definition records in C21 instead have four cells and grow during expansion.
declarations: asm-rec-size; asm-cap; asm-labels; asm-count; asm-base; asm-ip; asm-pass
phase: source loading allocates/initializes; pass 1 fills; pass 2 reads
state_owner: label table, target base, IP and pass selection
mechanism: Three 8-byte cells per label separate borrowed name storage from the target-address value; base is initialized independently of later IP resets.
assumptions: Default base is 6291456 (0x600000); capacity is 8192 labels; a fresh pass 1 must clear count before appending.
declaration_notes: asm-rec-size (constant, L158-L158): sets each three-cell label record to 24 bytes; asm-cap (constant, L159-L159): sets label capacity to 8192 records; asm-labels (create, L160-L160): reserves the array of name-address, name-length and target-IP triples; asm-count (variable, L161-L161): counts valid label records and survives the rewind between passes; asm-base (variable, L171-L171): holds the target address corresponding to output offset zero; asm-ip (variable, L173-L173): holds the target address of the next counted or emitted byte, independent of text cursor; asm-pass (variable, L174-L174): selects pass 1 sizing/storage or pass 2 resolution/emission
initialization_forms: L172: [lit] 6291456 asm-base ! sets the default target base to 0x600000; a load-time initialization form, not a colon definition
teaching_section: Reference: the label table borrows names and owns addresses

scope: Label-record addressing and append with borrowed name
interface_notes: The label text address is not the target address stored at record offset 16.
state_owner: label table and count
mechanism: Address arithmetic chooses the next 24-byte slot, writes its name slice/current target IP, then publishes the incremented count.
assumptions: Name bytes belong to expanded text and must outlive pass-2 lookup; append beyond capacity exits 242.
declaration_notes: asm-rec (colon, L177-L177): computes asm-labels plus index times the 24-byte record size; asm-store-label (colon, L180-L187): checks the next record count, borrows name address/length, stores current IP and increments count
teaching_section: Reference: the label table borrows names and owns addresses

scope: Newest-first label search and exact slice comparison
interface_notes: C21 definition lookup also scans backward but can see only preceding definitions.
state_owner: label lookup scratch and completed label table
mechanism: Reverse scanning implements newest declaration wins across the complete table, with length checked before byte comparison.
assumptions: Duplicate labels are not rejected; all pass-1 declarations are visible during every pass-2 lookup; scratch makes this a non-reentrant helper.
declaration_notes: asm-find-addr (variable, L189-L189): holds the borrowed query-name address during label lookup; asm-find-len (variable, L190-L190): holds query-name length during label lookup; asm-find-label (colon, L195-L210): scans the completed table newest first, checks length before bytes and returns IP/true or zero/false
teaching_section: Reference: the label table borrows names and owns addresses

scope: Hex character recognition and digit-value conversion
interface_notes: C22 uses recognition in pass 1 and conversion for already-validated bare pairs in pass 2.
state_owner: stateless character helpers
mechanism: Hex spelling and digit value are separate interfaces: recognition protects the bare-hex path, while conversion assumes a valid digit.
assumptions: hex-val does not validate; numeric-parser calls are not guarded by asm-hex-char?.
declaration_notes: hex-val (colon, L218-L227): converts a valid decimal or upper/lowercase hex character to a value from zero through fifteen; asm-hex-char? (colon, L231-L234): recognizes exactly decimal digits and A-F/a-f for the bare-hex validation path
teaching_section: Convert digits only under a valid-input contract

scope: Numeric-parser scratch state and bounded valid-input conversion contract
interface_notes: C21 teaches spelling/conversion; C22 chooses numeric fit bounds and emitted field width.
declarations: asm-dec-addr; asm-dec-len; asm-dec-val; asm-dec-neg; asm-dec-hex; asm-dec-i; asm-parse-number
state_owner: number-parser scratch cells
mechanism: The parser accumulates value times ten or sixteen plus digit value, after optional sign/prefix consumption, then applies a negative sign.
assumptions: Use well-formed bounded decimal or 0x/0X hex; no digit validation, required-digit check or cell-overflow diagnosis is supplied; leading zero alone remains decimal.
declaration_notes: asm-dec-addr (variable, L236-L236): holds the numeric input body address during conversion; asm-dec-len (variable, L237-L237): holds numeric input body length; asm-dec-val (variable, L238-L238): accumulates the numeric value by multiply-by-radix and add; asm-dec-neg (variable, L239-L239): records whether conversion consumed a leading minus; asm-dec-hex (variable, L240-L240): records whether conversion consumed a 0x or 0X prefix; asm-dec-i (variable, L241-L241): tracks the next body character after optional sign and prefix; asm-parse-number (colon, L248-L293): resets conversion state, consumes optional minus and hex prefix, accumulates decimal or hex digits and applies the sign
teaching_section: Trace the whole number parser

scope: Low-byte-first variable-width output
interface_notes: Uses asm-emit-byte for each capacity-checked output append.
state_owner: output sink and value/width on the data stack
mechanism: Repeated low-byte stores and unsigned division expose little-endian order and preserve the low two's-complement bytes of negative cell values.
assumptions: Widths are bounded by dispatch; only low width bytes are emitted, so accepted wide values can truncate.
declaration_notes: asm-emit-le (colon, L296-L303): writes the low byte repeatedly, unsigned-divides the cell by 256 and stops after the requested width
teaching_section: Reference: emit low bytes without changing their meaning

scope: Whitespace/comment skipping through LF or EOF
interface_notes: The token reader chooses quote handling after this skip.
phase: token acquisition during expansion and both assembly passes
state_owner: active cursor
mechanism: Whitespace and comment skipping stops at the next token; a comment ends at LF or EOF, even when attached directly to a preceding bare token.
assumptions: Whitespace is exactly space, tab, LF and CR; # and semicolon are comment markers only outside the quoted-token scan.
declaration_notes: asm-skip-rest-of-line (colon, L310-L314): consumes through LF or stops at EOF, allowing a trailing comment without a newline; asm-skip-ws (colon, L317-L327): skips space/tab/LF/CR and comments beginning with # or semicolon before the next token
teaching_section: Skip only the separators this implementation recognizes

scope: Quoted/bare token scans and borrowed token slices
interface_notes: Raw-token slices feed definition expansion; expanded-token slices feed C22 processing.
declarations: asm-tok-start; asm-tok-len; asm-quote-char; asm-read-quoted; asm-read-bareword; asm-read-token
phase: token acquisition during expansion and both assembly passes
state_owner: token-slice scratch; borrowed active-buffer bytes
mechanism: The first token character chooses quote or bare scanning; returned lengths include quote delimiters and token bytes are never copied by this reader.
assumptions: No escape handling or missing-close diagnostic; successful quoted examples supply matching delimiters; quote characters inside a bare token do not switch modes.
declaration_notes: asm-tok-start (variable, L329-L329): holds the borrowed start address of the token being read; asm-tok-len (variable, L330-L330): counts the token bytes returned to the caller, including quote delimiters; asm-quote-char (variable, L331-L331): remembers which opening quote must terminate the quoted token; asm-read-quoted (colon, L335-L342): consumes the opening quote and bytes through its matching close, including interior whitespace and comment characters; asm-read-bareword (colon, L345-L352): counts bytes until whitespace, #, semicolon or EOF without consuming that delimiter; asm-read-token (colon, L358-L368): skips separators, returns zero/zero at EOF, then selects quoted or bare scanning and returns a borrowed slice
teaching_section: A quote gets its special role at token start

scope: Current-token address/length staging shared with C22 dispatch
interface_notes: C22 owns dispatch and consumers; C21 owns the numeric classifier using this interface.
state_owner: borrowed expanded-token address/length
mechanism: These two cells keep a stable token slice available while classification, reference slicing and diagnostics call other helpers.
assumptions: A nonempty token is installed by asm-process-token before dependent helpers read it; expanded input remains alive.
declaration_notes: asm-token-start-tmp (variable, L374-L374): stages the current expanded token address for classification and C22 dispatch; asm-token-len-tmp (variable, L375-L375): stages the current expanded token length for body slices and field processing
teaching_section: The classifier inspects one body character

scope: Explicit-base scan and hex-emission index state
interface_notes: asm-find-gt and asm-check-hex/asm-do-hex explain their updates.
phase: assembly field parsing and bare-hex processing
state_owner: explicit-base scan scratch and hex-pair index
mechanism: Independent indices distinguish a token scan for > from bare-hex character validation and pair emission.
assumptions: These scratch cells do not own text or persist a separate parse tree.
declaration_notes: asm-gt-pos (variable, L376-L376): stores explicit-base separator position measured within the sigil body, or minus one when absent; asm-scan-i (variable, L377-L377): tracks the token index while searching for the explicit-base separator; asm-hex-i (variable, L378-L378): tracks characters while validating or emitting bare hex pairs
teaching_section: An explicit base names the subtraction point

scope: Numeric-versus-label body classification
interface_notes: C22 uses the decision for generic fields and to guard the explicit-base percent branch.
state_owner: staged token slice
mechanism: The first body character alone selects numeric parsing; a digit/minus body is not first looked up as a label.
assumptions: Leading plus is not numeric; digit/minus-leading label spellings are unsafe for references; classification does not prove valid digits.
declaration_notes: asm-tok-numeric? (colon, L382-L388): classifies a nonempty sigil body as numeric only when its first character is a decimal digit or minus
teaching_section: The classifier inspects one body character

scope: Locate explicit-base separator, with no-separator sentinel
interface_notes: Only nonnumeric percent-reference handling gives this separator special meaning.
state_owner: explicit-base separator position and scan index
mechanism: Record the first > as a body-relative index so two borrowed name slices can be formed without modifying text.
assumptions: No separator is represented by true, which is minus one in this Forth; this scan supplies no name validation.
declaration_notes: asm-find-gt (colon, L391-L401): searches from token index one for the first > and records its body-relative index; otherwise writes true, the minus-one sentinel
teaching_section: An explicit base names the subtraction point

scope: Store declarations in pass 1 only
interface_notes: Uses the same current-token slice established by dispatch.
state_owner: label table
mechanism: The leading colon contributes no width: strip it, then associate the remaining name slice with the current target IP.
assumptions: Pass 2 does nothing for declarations; duplicate names are retained and resolved by reverse lookup.
declaration_notes: asm-do-label-decl (colon, L404-L409): removes the colon from the token slice and stores the name/current IP only in pass 1
teaching_section: Reference: the label table borrows names and owns addresses

scope: Token diagnostic path and distinct fit-policy contract
interface_notes: C21 parser limitations remain separate from C22 fit checking.
phase: token failure during validation or resolution
state_owner: diagnostic fd 2 and process exit status
mechanism: Token failures attempt to print the token and one LF before exit; the adjacent contract distinguishes numeric bounds from label bounds.
assumptions: Diagnostic writes are unchecked; capacity failures use die directly rather than this token-print path; the table comments are bounded to the implemented field policy.
declaration_notes: asm-tok-err (colon, L412-L415): attempts token and LF writes to fd 2 before terminating with its supplied code
teaching_section: Failures have a phase as well as a code

scope: Range state, width half-range, label/numeric limits and fit gate
interface_notes: A value passing this policy can still truncate to the emitted width; !256 yields low byte 00.
declarations: asm-fit-lo; asm-fit-hi; asm-half; asm-label-bounds; asm-number-bounds; asm-fit
state_owner: inclusive range-bound scratch cells
mechanism: Half-range arithmetic produces the actual label/numeric limits; the fit gate skips all width-four checks rather than imposing an invented 32-bit range.
assumptions: Label relative bounds are signed; numeric limits deliberately differ, including !-129 through !256; use bounded cell arithmetic and the stated 1-4-byte widths.
declaration_notes: asm-fit-lo (variable, L428-L428): holds the selected inclusive low fit limit; asm-fit-hi (variable, L429-L429): holds the selected inclusive high fit limit; asm-half (colon, L433-L440): forms 128 * 256^(width - 1) for the bounded widths used by reference dispatch; asm-label-bounds (colon, L444-L451): sets signed bounds for relative label fields or zero through twice-half minus one for absolute fields; asm-number-bounds (colon, L456-L462): sets the source-specific numeric lower bound to minus-half minus one and doubles the upper half for width one or absolute fields; asm-fit (colon, L466-L472): preserves width/value on success; checks stored bounds only when width is less than four and emits a token error if a checked value is outside them
teaching_section: Accepted values are not quite the usual field ranges

scope: Sigil/reference contracts and token-body slice
interface_notes: Widths/modes: !1 relative, @2 relative, ~3 relative, %4 relative, $2 absolute, &4 absolute.
state_owner: current token slice and field-format parameters
mechanism: The sigil determines fixed width and label-relative/absolute interpretation, while asm-ref-name exposes the body without the sigil.
assumptions: Numeric bodies are immediates even for relative sigils; only percent gains explicit-base label subtraction.
declaration_notes: asm-ref-name (colon, L490-L490): returns the current token slice after its one-byte sigil
teaching_section: Reference: six sigils, three meanings

scope: Count then resolve numeric/label reference, relative field-end arithmetic
interface_notes: Undefined-name exit code is a dispatcher parameter; 244 denotes label fit and 245 numeric fit.
state_owner: IP, completed labels, fit bounds and output
mechanism: Known widths permit sizing before lookup; pass 2 subtracts IP plus width for relative labels, never for numeric immediates.
assumptions: An undefined label or fit failure can stop pass 2 after pass 1 succeeded; token-boundary IP agreement requires unchanged input and successful processing.
declaration_notes: asm-do-ref (colon, L496-L517): counts width in pass 1; in pass 2 converts a number or looks up a label, applies field-end subtraction only for relative labels, checks the chosen bounds and emits
teaching_section: Reference: six sigils, three meanings

scope: Explicit two-label difference and generic percent fallback
interface_notes: Numeric percent bodies bypass > splitting; ordinary %label uses undefined-name code 234.
phase: assembly pass 1 sizing; pass 2 percent resolution
state_owner: two borrowed label names, IP and output
mechanism: The explicit form computes target minus base, without field-IP subtraction, and otherwise falls back to the ordinary four-byte relative form.
assumptions: Explicit-base syntax requires two labels; target is checked first (233), then base (232); width-four results emit low four bytes without fit checking.
declaration_notes: asm-do-pct-ref (colon, L521-L541): resolves two labels for nonnumeric pass-2 %target>base, emits their difference, or delegates to the generic four-byte relative handler
teaching_section: An explicit base names the subtraction point

scope: Bare-hex validation and even-length invariant
interface_notes: This guards later bare-pair conversion, not C21 numeric conversion.
state_owner: hex scan index and staged token
mechanism: Checking characters before parity means a nonhex token fails 246; only an all-hex odd-length token reaches 247.
assumptions: Whole byte pairs must occur within each token; no nibble accumulation across whitespace; a misspelled name that is valid even-length hex can be bytes.
declaration_notes: asm-check-hex (colon, L547-L559): checks every character before checking even length, using 246 for a nonhex character and 247 for odd valid-hex length
teaching_section: Reference: the pass loop gives every token one owner

scope: Bare-hex count in pass 1, pair decoding/emission in pass 2
interface_notes: The shared invariant is IP equals base plus emitted count at successful pass-2 token boundaries.
state_owner: IP, bare-hex index and output sink
mechanism: A token of two-n characters counts n in pass 1 and emits exactly n combined high/low nibble bytes in pass 2.
assumptions: Pass 2 relies on validation of the identical expanded text during pass 1.
declaration_notes: asm-do-hex (colon, L563-L579): validates and counts pairs in pass 1; in pass 2 combines high/low nibbles and advances output position and IP for each byte
teaching_section: Reference: the pass loop gives every token one owner

scope: First-character token dispatch and undefined-label code parameters
interface_notes: Undefined-name codes: &231, %234, !235, @236, ~237, $238; percent explicit-base cases use 232/233.
state_owner: staged token and handler parameters
mechanism: First-character dispatch chooses label/sigil handling; every other nonempty token reaches the bare-hex path.
assumptions: Only the six listed sigils are implemented; no ISA decoder or ELF validation determines field choice.
declaration_notes: asm-process-token (colon, L584-L594): stages a nonempty token, dispatches colon and six sigils with their widths/modes/error codes, and otherwise chooses bare hex
teaching_section: Reference: the pass loop gives every token one owner

scope: Pass loop and initial IP/label-count reset
interface_notes: C21 owns asm-read-token; C22 composes its nonempty slices with dispatch.
phase: assembly pass initialization and token walking
state_owner: pass flag, IP, label count and active cursor
mechanism: One loop serves both passes; initial IP/count reset belongs before pass 1, while the driver performs a narrower reset before pass 2.
assumptions: Loop termination uses returned length zero; asm-init does not choose a buffer, rewind its cursor or initialize output position.
declaration_notes: asm-pass-loop (colon, L600-L605): reads tokens until zero length and dispatches each nonempty token under the current pass flag; asm-init (colon, L607-L609): copies base into IP and clears the label count before pass 1, which is why it must not be reused at the pass-2 rewind
teaching_section: Reference: the pass loop gives every token one owner

scope: One-pass expansion contract and definition record/table storage
interface_notes: C22 label records have three cells and are complete before their lookups begin.
state_owner: definition table borrowing raw input
mechanism: Four 8-byte fields preserve name/body slices; only preceding definitions have been stored when a use is encountered in the single raw walk.
assumptions: Capacity is 4096 records; definition replacement is one pass, not recursive macro rescanning.
declaration_notes: asm-def-rec-size (constant, L621-L621): sets each four-cell definition record to 32 bytes; asm-def-cap (constant, L622-L622): sets definition capacity to 4096 records; asm-defs (create, L623-L623): reserves records borrowing raw name/body slices rather than copying their text; asm-def-count (variable, L624-L624): counts only definitions already encountered in the one-way raw-input walk
teaching_section: Lay out one record completely

scope: Definition indexing and bounded four-cell record append
interface_notes: DEFINE dispatch obtains two further tokens and passes their slices here.
state_owner: definition records and count
mechanism: The next 32-byte slot receives body length/address and name length/address before the incremented count makes it searchable.
assumptions: Raw input remains unchanged; appending beyond 4096 records fails 243; the storage helper does not validate name/body grammar.
declaration_notes: asm-def-rec (colon, L626-L626): computes asm-defs plus index times the 32-byte definition record size; asm-def-store (colon, L630-L638): checks capacity, stores raw name address/length and body address/length at offsets 0/8/16/24, then increments count
teaching_section: Lay out one record completely

scope: Newest preceding definition lookup
interface_notes: C22 reverse label search instead sees the entire completed table.
state_owner: definition lookup scratch and currently stored records
mechanism: Reverse search lets a later preceding DEFINE shadow an earlier one, then returns the body slice for one literal copy.
assumptions: Definitions appearing after a use cannot retroactively change it; scratch is reused rather than reentrant; missing lookup returns three zeros.
declaration_notes: asm-deff-addr (variable, L640-L640): holds the borrowed query-name address during definition lookup; asm-deff-len (variable, L641-L641): holds query-name length during definition lookup; asm-def-find (colon, L645-L660): scans definitions already stored newest first, checks exact length/bytes and returns body slice/true or zero/zero/false
teaching_section: Search backward through what exists now

scope: Stored DEFINE keyword and exact keyword recognition
interface_notes: The driver tests DEFINE before handling direct strings or user-defined names.
phase: source loading initializes keyword; expansion tests tokens
state_owner: six keyword bytes and candidate slice
mechanism: Length guards an exact six-byte comparison, making DEFINE case-sensitive and distinct from ordinary definition lookup.
assumptions: Keyword bytes are not a NUL-terminated string; lowercase define takes the ordinary-token path.
declaration_notes: asm-define-kw (create, L663-L663): creates the six literal bytes DEFINE without a required NUL terminator; asm-is-define? (colon, L666-L671): requires length six and exact byte equality with the stored uppercase keyword
teaching_section: Dispatch once, then move on

scope: Expansion-copy scratch state and counted byte copying
interface_notes: Both unexpanded ordinary tokens and matched definition bodies use this helper.
state_owner: copy scratch and expanded-text sink
mechanism: A counted copy appends the supplied source slice without recursively interpreting what its copied bytes spell.
assumptions: Caller decides separators; the helper itself neither appends a separator nor rescans a copied quote or alias.
declaration_notes: asm-cp-addr (variable, L673-L673): holds the input slice address during literal copying or direct-string translation; asm-cp-len (variable, L674-L674): holds that slice length, including delimiters for a quoted token; asm-cp-i (variable, L675-L675): holds the next copy/translation index, starting at zero for ordinary bytes and one after a quote opener; asm-exp-bytes (colon, L678-L686): copies exactly the supplied slice into expanded storage via checked byte appends; it does not rescan definitions
teaching_section: Later session: open the two copy operations

scope: Nibble-to-uppercase-hex character encoding
interface_notes: Only the direct double-quote encoder splits body bytes into these nibbles.
state_owner: stateless nibble-to-text conversion
mechanism: Map each nibble to its uppercase text digit so a body byte can be represented by two characters in expanded input.
assumptions: Input must be a nibble 0-15; this is the inverse representation direction from hex-val.
declaration_notes: asm-hex-digit (colon, L689-L694): maps a nibble from zero through fifteen to uppercase ASCII hex spelling
teaching_section: Encode a body as hexadecimal text

scope: Direct double-quote body encoding and NUL terminator
interface_notes: A quoted DEFINE body copied by asm-exp-bytes does not enter this direct-string branch.
state_owner: copy scratch, raw quoted slice and expanded text
mechanism: Each body byte grows into two uppercase hex digits plus space; an extra 00 token requests the eventual terminating zero byte.
assumptions: Input slice includes two matched delimiters; no escapes are decoded; byte encodings are not emitted machine bytes yet.
declaration_notes: asm-exp-string-double (colon, L700-L714): skips matched delimiters, encodes each body byte as two uppercase hex characters plus space, then appends 00 and space
teaching_section: Encode a body as hexadecimal text

scope: Direct single-quote verbatim text insertion
interface_notes: This is a direct-token path; copied quoted definition bodies retain their quote characters.
state_owner: copy scratch, raw quoted slice and expanded text
mechanism: Remove two matched delimiters and insert the body as text plus one separator, allowing multiple later assembly tokens in that body.
assumptions: No implicit NUL is added; interior whitespace/comment characters are copied and may be interpreted by the next assembly-token reader.
declaration_notes: asm-exp-string-single (colon, L718-L727): skips matched delimiters, copies the body as text unchanged and appends one space without adding a NUL token
teaching_section: Copy a body as text

scope: Expansion driver, definition/quote/macro dispatch and separators
interface_notes: Output keeps numeric sigils and symbolic labels for C22; this internal stream is not stock M1 fully lowered hex2 output.
phase: one expansion walk over raw input
state_owner: definition state and expanded-text output
mechanism: Dispatch order is DEFINE, direct double quote, direct single quote, then one newest-preceding definition lookup or literal copy.
assumptions: Caller selected raw input; DEFINE consumes two tokens without completeness checks; copied bodies are not rescanned; capacity errors can stop expansion.
declaration_notes: asm-expand-pass (colon, L731-L762): clears expansion length and definition count, consumes raw tokens once, handles DEFINE/direct quotes before one definition lookup, then separates copied ordinary tokens
teaching_section: Dispatch once, then move on

scope: Output-path data, three-walk driver, reset boundary and caller invocation contract
interface_notes: The driver performs three token walks: expansion, sizing and emission. A supplied ELF envelope, if any, is part of input rather than manufactured here.
phase: source loading creates path; driver orchestrates load/expand/two passes/store
state_owner: raw/expanded/output buffers, tables, cursor, IP and process
mechanism: The complete reset sequence preserves expanded bytes and label table between counting and emission, then attempts the fixed-path write and exits.
assumptions: The source file defines asm-main without invoking it; caller must invoke after the Forth prelude and separate it from assembly input; pre-output failure can leave an older path untouched.
declaration_notes: asm-out-path (create, L765-L765): creates twelve path characters /tmp/asm-out followed by one NUL byte, thirteen bytes total; asm-main (colon, L767-L781): loads, expands, counts labels, rewinds while preserving labels, emits, attempts output storage and exits the seed process
teaching_section: Reference: the caller starts three walks, not two expansions
